answers.explanation: Demand above capacity means the queue never drains.
With one server, one crash is a total outage. Scaling out removes that.
Requests at the back of the queue wait longest, so the tail moves first.
Health checks notice a dead server and the rest keep serving.
Synchronous replication waits for the standby on every write, so it loses nothing but adds latency.
Crash the database in Chaos mode and everything fails.
